entries.effect: the class is there and names worlds as the release's does: +pageWorld and +defaultClientWorld are each one object for the process, +worldWithName: gives the same object back for the same name, and -name answers the name for a named world and nil for the two standard ones. What a world stands for - a separate JavaScript context - the release does not have: its UIWebView runs one context per frame, so scripts of every world share the page's globals

entries.reason: the whole of this API is that window.webkit.messageHandlers.<name>.postMessage() answers a JavaScript Promise the page awaits. The JavaScriptCore of 6.1.3 has no Promise: the armv7 shared cache of the release holds the string Promise twice, both of them the Objective-C selector initWithDataPromise: of a system class, and none of JSPromise, PromiseConstructor or promiseCapability, where the cache of 9.3 holds 657. A page on this release therefore has nothing to receive a reply with, and a handler that could never be replied to is worse than one that is not there
